title: duck-ui real-corpus content-compile benchmark: velite vs @gentleduck/md (dmc), cold vs warm cache

methodology.measured_step: content-compile only (not the full `next build`): the CLI invocation that turns apps/duck/content/**/*.mdx into the generated JSON collections consumed by the app.
methodology.timer: wall-clock (bash `date +%s%N` around the process), full process including runtime startup

cold_definition.dmc: `duck-md clean` (removes apps/duck/.gentleduck/.cache) run immediately before the timed build
cold_definition.velite: `--clean` flag; velite has no persistent cache so every run is architecturally cold

methodology.warm_definition: dmc only: `duck-md build` run again immediately after a prior build, reusing apps/duck/.gentleduck/.cache/dmc
methodology.runner_note: invoked via /usr/bin/node directly, not `bun`; duck-md.mjs's TS-config re-exec path (spawns `process.execPath` to run the tsx loader) assumes Node semantics and crashes under Bun's execPath on this host -- see caveats

duck_ui.new_commit_subject: fix(registry-examples): fix crash in primitives-vs-radix benchmark chart
duck_ui.migration_commit_subject: chore(docs): migrate duck site content pipeline from velite to @gentleduck/md

corpus.note: corpus grew 41% between the two commits; numbers below are NOT normalized per-file, they compare the real historical corpus at each point in time

dmc_cache_hit_rate.note: 6 misses persisted across every warm run; cache never reaches 100% hit rate on this corpus

caveats: velite has no persistent cache; its three runs (215.4s, 218.3s, 225.3s) show no warm-up trend, confirming every velite build is architecturally cold
corpus size differs (366 vs 516 files) because content grew between the two commits; dmc is processing 41% more content and is still ~40-73x faster

each number includes Node process startup, TS config loading, and (for dmc) shiki/syntect highlighter init -- this is real end-to-end CLI time a developer would feel, not a microbenchmark of the parser alone

n=3 for cold runs, n=5 for warm; see duck-benchmarks/GUIDE.md for how the existing phase-1..7 benchmarks treat sample-size/stddev -- this phase is a smaller, real-corpus spot-check rather than a 200-sample statistical run

running `duck-md build` via `bun` directly fails on this host with `Cannot find module './cjs/index.cjs' from ''`; root cause is duck-md.mjs's loadConfig() re-exec-under-tsx path using process.execPath (which under Bun is the bun binary, not node) to spawn tsx's Node-oriented CLI loader. Running via a real Node binary (/usr/bin/node) works correctly and is what was used for every measurement in this file.
